terra.problem: The comparison does not clearly connect the animals' pasture with a counter and cooling rack. The joke's logic doesn't click.
The text says the region was suitable for livestock, not that grass caught their eyes.
Grapes are mentioned as food outside a Bible fact or an answer on the card.
Saying he would be nervous 'too' implies the Gadites and Reubenites were nervous, which the text does not say.
The text does not say they are standing in the land, and their request not to cross is not the same as saying they want to stay out of Canaan altogether.
The categorical statement that none of the men twenty or older will see the land omits the two exceptions Moses gives in the next verse.
Verse 2 says the Gadites and Reubenites came to Moses, Eleazar and the leaders, not that Moses was talking to Eleazar. It also does not place Eleazar in a room.
The drawer joke compares Papa's experience with the wilderness judgment immediately after mentioning the generation that died, making light of a heavy consequence.
The text specifies that the generation who had done evil in the LORD's sight was gone. 'That whole generation was gone' leaves out that qualification.
The explanation says the reward is simply going home, omitting the possession of the land, which Moses also promises.
The Gadites and Reubenites have already made their promise before Moses gives this warning, so 'before they promise' is incorrect.
'Right away' and 'on the spot' add timing the text does not give.
'Not a single one stays behind' goes beyond the promise about men equipped for war; their children are to remain.
The verse gives land to the half-tribe of Manasseh; it does not establish where every member of the other half settles.
Driving out the Amorites is not the only action the verse names: the descendants also go to Gilead and capture it.
